fact: The reefer loading and excursion procedure is document KC-OPS-SOP-031, currently revision 6.
Revision 6 of SOP KC-OPS-SOP-031 took effect on 2 September 2024.
Revision 6 of the reefer SOP replaces revision 5, which was dated 17 March 2023.
Revision 6 of the reefer SOP was written by Wacław Bielicki, senior shift supervisor at GDY-1.
Jarek Lindqvist approved revision 6 of the reefer SOP on 28 August 2024.
The reefer SOP is valid at all five Korvane depots.
Wacław Bielicki started working on the quay at Gdynia in 2004.
Under revision 5 of the SOP the pre-cool for chilled loads was 3 hours.
Under revision 5 of the SOP the loading window for chilled boxes was 45 minutes.
The excursion ladder gained a fourth rung in revision 6 because of the incident on 14 June.
The pre-cool clock for an empty box starts when Tidewalk shows the first setpoint reached message for that box.
Chilled and pharma loads use a setpoint band of +2.0 to +8.0 °C.
Chilled general cargo needs a minimum pre-cool of 4.5 hours.
For chilled general cargo the box's PTI sticker must not be older than 14 days.
values: PTI sticker not older than 14 days

fact: Frozen loads have a setpoint of −18.0 °C or colder and need a minimum pre-cool of 9 hours.
Pharma / GDP loads need a minimum pre-cool of 6 hours.
For pharma loads return air must be within ±0.5 °C of setpoint for the last 60 minutes of pre-cooling.
values: within ±0.5 °C of setpoint for the last 60 minutes

fact: If the yard is warmer than 28 °C when the unit is plugged in, 90 minutes are added to every pre-cool time.
Before the pre-cool clock starts the drain plugs and T-floor must be checked, because standing water in the box is not acceptable.
Chilled goods may be loaded only at a core temperature of +6.0 °C or colder.
Frozen goods are loaded at a core temperature of −15.0 °C or colder.
Frozen product between −15.0 and −12.0 °C may be loaded only with a signed waiver from the customer's representative.
Frozen product warmer than −12.0 °C must be refused, photographed and reported to Duty Ops.
Maximum pallet height, including cargo, is 2.18 m in a 40' high-cube.
Maximum pallet height is 2.06 m in a 20' or a standard-height 40' container.
The height limits leave at least 12 cm of air above the top layer for return air.
A 40' reefer may take at most 23 euro-pallets and a 20' at most 10.
Pharma loads are limited to 20 pallets in a 40' container.
No pallet may weigh more than 1,180 kg gross.
A gap of 8 cm must be left between the last pallet and the doors and 4 cm to each side wall.
The first 20 cm in front of the unit bulkhead must be kept completely clear of cartons.
values: first 20 cm in front of the unit bulkhead

fact: Three KC-Tag 4 loggers go into every 40' load and two into every 20'.
Tag 1, the door tag, goes in a carton on the top layer of the second pallet from the doors on the kerb side, about 20 cm in from the wall.
The Tag 1 position is the warmest spot in the box.
Tag 2, the middle tag, goes at the centre of the load on the middle pallet at roughly 1.1 m height, and is left out in a 20'.
values: In a 20' this tag is left out

fact: Tag 3, the nose tag, goes in the bottom layer of the pallet nearest the unit, about 30 cm off the floor.
The Tag 3 position is the coldest spot and serves as the freeze-damage detector.
A KC-Tag 4 is activated by holding its button for 4 seconds until the green LED blinks twice.
An activated tag must show online on the KC-Hub 200 within 90 seconds or be replaced.
No tag whose battery is under 2.85 V may be used.
The tag logging interval is 5 minutes by default, 10 minutes for frozen and 2 minutes for pharma loads.
The hand probe is inserted into the first, a middle and the last pallet loaded, and the three readings go on the form.
values: first, a middle and the last pallet

fact: The loading window is timed with the stopwatch kept on the dock clipboard.
The loading window for chilled cargo is 38 minutes with the yard up to 25 °C and 30 minutes above 25 °C.
The loading window for frozen cargo is 24 minutes up to 25 °C and 18 minutes above 25 °C.
The loading window for pharma / GDP cargo is 16 minutes up to 25 °C and 12 minutes above 25 °C.
Loading through a curtain-only door counts every minute twice on the stopwatch.
After the doors are shut, each re-opening is limited to 4 minutes and three re-opens per load per day shift.
values: three re-opens per load per day shift

fact: A fourth re-open of a load in one day shift needs the supervisor's name on the form.
The reefer unit stays on with fans on high during loading, and any manual defrost must finish at least 40 minutes before the first pallet.
After exceeding the loading window, Tag 1 must be watched closely for the next 2 hours.
Out-of-band minutes accumulate over a rolling 24 hours, and a total of 3 hours 15 minutes makes the load Red.
Amber (Level 1) is triggered for standard cargo by more than 1.5 °C above setpoint for 20 minutes and for pharma cargo by more than 0.8 °C for 10 minutes.
At Amber the shift supervisor on site checks the unit alarm code, door seals and setpoint, makes no external call, and re-reads the tag every 15 minutes.
values: unit alarm code, door seals and setpoint

fact: Orange (Level 2) is triggered for standard cargo by more than 3.0 °C for 45 minutes and for pharma cargo by more than 1.5 °C for 20 minutes.
At Orange the supervisor rings Duty Ops on ext 2000 within 10 minutes.
At Orange the fleet workshop on ext 2750 prepares a swap box and a HOLD-Y sticker goes on the box.
Red (Level 3) is triggered for standard cargo by more than 5.0 °C for 90 minutes and for pharma cargo by more than 2.5 °C for 40 minutes.
At Red, Duty Ops and Quality on-call Benedikta Aaltonen (ext 2620) are called.
At Red the account manager phones the customer within 60 minutes and the load carries a HOLD-R sticker that only Quality can release.
Black (Level 4) is triggered for standard cargo by a single reading above +12.0 °C or more than 6 hours in total.
For pharma cargo, Black is triggered by any reading outside +2.0 to +8.0 °C lasting more than 90 minutes.
values: any reading outside +2.0 to +8.0 °C for more than 90 minutes

fact: At Black, Jarek Lindqvist (ext 2010) is phoned in the same hour and Legal (Sofia Brandão) is told.
At Black, Quality notifies the insurance broker within 24 hours.
Duty Ops issues the incident number for a Black excursion in the format EX-2024-nnnn.
On a chilled load any tag below +0.5 °C for 30 minutes goes straight to Orange.
At every level it is forbidden to change the setpoint, to open the doors to look, or to take a tag out of the box to reset it.
values: take a tag out of the box

fact: In January 2013 at Gdynia it hit −23 °C overnight, the sockets on pad B froze, and 14 boxes of fish went to Red.
The 14 June excursion that triggered the fourth ladder level lasted nine hours.
Every load gets a form KC-OPS-114, the Loading and Excursion Record, filled in Tidewalk on the dock tablet.
A paper KC-OPS-114 used while the tablets are dead must be keyed into Tidewalk by the end of that shift.
values: by the end of that shift

fact: Form KC-OPS-114 must show the container number, the photographed bolt seal number, the three tag IDs with positions, the pre-cool start and end times, the loading window stopwatch time and the three hand-probe readings.
At least four photographs are required: the load pattern from the rear, the top gap under the red line, the tags in place, and the seal.
After a Level 2 or higher excursion the tag data must be downloaded within 2 hours.
For Level 3 and Level 4 an Excursion Report goes into Tidewalk under ticket category EXC within 24 hours.
For a Level 4 excursion the full 8D root-cause report is due within 10 working days.
Loading records are kept 7 years, and GDP files are kept 12 years.
Both the loader and the supervisor sign KC-OPS-114, and Quality audits roughly one form in twelve.
values: The loader and the supervisor both sign

The depot safety manual is document KC-QHS-001, version 4.2, issued on 4 March 2024.
The depot safety manual is owned by Quality & Compliance under Benedikta Aaltonen.
The depot safety manual was approved by Dieter Ahlbeck-Roe, the COO.

The master copy of the safety manual is in the Tidewalk document library under QHS/001.
The safety manual is to be read together with SOP KC-OPS-SOP-031 on reefer loading and KC-OPS-SOP-044 on refrigerant leaks.
Where national or local law is stricter than the safety manual the law prevails.

The safety manual is reviewed every 12 months and the next review is due by 31 March 2025.

Each depot elects one safety steward for every 25 employees on a given shift pattern, rounded up.
values: one safety steward for every 25 employees

fact: Safety stewards serve a 2-year term, complete 16 hours of steward training in their first quarter and get 2 paid hours a week to walk the site.
Anyone on site may stop an operation they believe is dangerous by showing the orange STOP card or shouting STOP.
There were 11 stop-work events in 2023, a number the Company considers too low.
The Safety Committee meets every 6 weeks under the chair of Benedikta Aaltonen.
The Safety Committee has a quorum of 4 members, at least one of whom must be an elected steward.
Safety Committee minutes are posted in Tidewalk within 5 working days.
The Safety Committee reviews every incident of category B or worse.
A contractor may not start work without a permit-to-work signed by the depot manager or the shift supervisor on duty.
values: permit-to-work signed by the depot manager or the shift supervisor on duty

fact: The induction for new employees and agency workers takes 3 hours 40 minutes on the first day.

Helmets may be left off only inside a vehicle cab or inside a building.

At −16 °C to −25 °C the maximum continuous time is 45 minutes followed by a 15-minute rest.
Colder than −25 °C the maximum continuous time is 30 minutes followed by a 20-minute rest.
Work below −25 °C is never done alone, and the person outside the room holds a radio and the stopwatch.

Lone workers check in by radio every 40 minutes, and a missed check-in is chased within 5 minutes.
